jess_support: Hey @customer_sam — I can see repeated 500s and some billing spikes on your project. Can you grab one or two request/trace IDs from the failing calls? We need the raw ID + an approximate UTC timestamp for correlation.

anil_mobile: For Android apps the simplest is to pull verbose SDK logs or add a small network interceptor. Look for the response header `x-redwood-request-id` (sometimes `x-request-id`).

lee_devex: If you have Console access you can also: Console -> Requests -> filter by user/email -> click the failing request -> copy the trace_id from the details pane. That trace_id maps to our logs.

customer_sam: I tried adb logcat but don't see a header. App uses OkHttp and Retrofit.

anil_mobile: If using OkHttp, add this interceptor temporarily to log the header:
```
class IdInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val request = chain.request()
    val response = chain.proceed(request)
    val id = response.header("x-redwood-request-id") ?: response.header("x-request-id")
    Log.d("Redwood", "req-id=$id status=${response.code}")
    return response
  }
}
```
Install the interceptor and reproduce the failing flow once. The log line will show the request id.

jess_support: If you can't modify the app, do a quick curl against the same endpoint (mask the API key) and include `-v` to surface response headers. Example repro curl (mask keys before sending):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
The server response headers will include `x-redwood-request-id`. Copy that value.

customer_sam: We do have a web client path too — should I capture a HAR?

lee_devex: Yes, please. From Chrome: Network tab -> reproduce -> right-click the failing request -> Save as HAR with content. That plus the timestamp is super helpful.

jess_support: For a debug bundle please include: 1) HAR or SDK logs, 2) the curl command you ran (with keys redacted), 3) approximate UTC timestamps for each failing request, 4) user id/session id, 5) which model/route and region (e.g., `gpt-jax / us-west`). Put everything in a single ZIP.
